name: hover-card-reaches-its-fit-width-on-the-first-hover
description:
the hover card is laid out inside the toast widget's own WebContents, which is sized from what the card itself reports - so a card could never report itself wider than the widget already was, and a first hover (nothing to grow from) clipped a correctly-elided middle-ellipsis fit with an END-style CSS ellipsis instead. This scenario hovers a long link ONCE, with no warm-up hover before it, since a second hover can succeed off a width the first one already established and would hide the defect.

textContent alone cannot catch the bug: CSS text-overflow:ellipsis clips the PAINTED box without touching the DOM text elideMiddle already set correctly. The real check is geometric - .ctl's scrollWidth (the full content, including anything CSS would hide) must not exceed its clientWidth (what is actually visible), which makes 'the CSS net never fires' measurable.

actions.note: past the show debounce the hover path keeps

actions.expression: (() => { const a = document.createElement('a'); a.href = 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ&list=PLtaskEightEightFive&index=1&t=42s'; a.textContent = a.href; a.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;left:0;top:0;width:100%;height:100%;z-index:99;background:rgba(0,0,0,.02)'; document.body.appendChild(a); return 'one full-viewport link'; })()
actions.note: a single link covering the whole card, so this hover is the FIRST one this page ever fires - no prior card to have already grown
the FIRST real pointer move in this run - no earlier hover to have already sized the widget

actions.expression: (() => { const t = document.querySelector('.toasts .toast .ctl'); return t ? String(t.textContent.includes('\u2026')) : 'no card'; })()
actions.note: The link is long enough that elideMiddle must shorten it

actions.expression: (() => { const t = document.querySelector('.toasts .toast .ctl'); return t ? t.textContent : 'no card'; })()
actions.note: diagnostic: the actual elided string, for the report

actions.expression: (() => { const full = 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ&list=PLtaskEightEightFive&index=1&t=42s'; const t = document.querySelector('.toasts .toast .ctl'); if (!t) { return 'no card'; } const shown = t.textContent; const parts = shown.split('\u2026'); if (parts.length !== 2) { return 'not one ellipsis: ' + shown; } const [pre, suf] = parts; return String(pre.length > 0 && suf.length > 0 && full.startsWith(pre) && full.endsWith(suf)); })()
actions.note: A MIDDLE ellipsis keeps both ends. A CSS end-ellipsis would instead leave the DOM text (which this reads) as the untouched full elideMiddle fit, so this alone cannot see an end-clip - the geometry check below does.

actions.expression: (() => { const t = document.querySelector('.toasts .toast .ctl'); if (!t) { return 'no card'; } return String(t.scrollWidth <= t.clientWidth + 1); })()
actions.note: ScrollWidth is the label's full content width including anything overflow:hidden is hiding. If it exceeds clientWidth (what is actually visible), the CSS safety net fired and end-clipped a fit that elideMiddle already got right.

actions.expression: (() => { const c = document.querySelector('.toasts .toast'); return c ? String(Math.round(c.getBoundingClientRect().width)) : 'no card'; })()
actions.note: diagnostic: the card's actual rendered width on the first hover, for the report

actions.expression: (() => { const t = document.querySelector('.toasts .toast .ctl'); return t ? (Math.round(t.scrollWidth) + '/' + Math.round(t.clientWidth)) : 'no card'; })()
actions.note: diagnostic: scrollWidth/clientWidth pair backing card-not-clipped-by-css, for the report
a screenshot of the first-hover card showing the middle ellipsis whole, not end-clipped
off the page onto the sidebar, which clears the card

assertions.desc: A middle ellipsis, both ends real substrings of the source URL
On the FIRST hover, the label's full content fits its visible box - the CSS ellipsis net never fired
